reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) strongly supports the formation of a protective, adherent Al2O3 scale via fluorine treatment on Ti-45Al-8.5Nb at 1000°C, but it provides no data on refractory high-entropy alloys, the specific mechanism of Al fluoride volatilization, or the claimed >70% improvement for RHEAs. The key premises about transferability, mechanism, and quantitative prediction for RHEAs are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Fluorine treatment promotes formation of a protective Al2O3 scale on TiAl alloys at 1000°C
The Al2O3 scale formed is continuous, adherent, and reduces oxidation mass gain
The fluorine effect can be transferred from TiAl intermetallics to refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) containing Al, Cr, Nb, Ta
Fluorine reacts with Al to form volatile Al fluorides that locally enrich Al and trigger selective Al2O3 formation
The treatment will yield >70% reduction in oxidation mass gain for RHEAs under the same conditions
